title: Paella Mixta
notes: The 'Mixta' or 'mixed' refers to the mixing of seafood with meat from land animals. Traditionally Paella could be solely land based or solely seafood based. A land based version could include green and white beans and artichokes with chicken, rabbit or even snails. A seafood based version would usually drop the beans and include any type of seafood. The word Paella is Valencian and means 'pan'. Generally Paella is considered a Spanish national dish but in Spain it's usually thought of as a regional specialty of Valencia.

ingredientSections.heading: Paella Mixta
items: 300g Chorizo Sausage, casings removed and crumbled
2 Red Pimientos, from a can or jar

methodSections.heading: Paella Mixta
steps: Heat up the stock in a saucepan and preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Season chicken and brown it with some oil in a paellera or large oven proof fry pan, remove from pan and set aside.
In the same pan add a touch more oil, the onion, garlic, green pepper, and tomatoes, season and keep stirring until mixture is cooked then add the chorizo toward the end.
Add hot lobster stock to the pan, stir in the rice, paprika and saffron and bring to a boil.
Arrange the chicken, prawns, clams, and mussels on the rice partially submerging them in the boiling liquid.
Lower heat and cook until stock is almost gone. Check to see if the rice is cooked and add a touch more stock or water if it is under-done.
Add green peas and strips of red pimientos.
Finish cooking in a hot oven at 220°C (425°F).
Decorate with lemon wedges and serve in the pan.
